title: Scale House Standing Instruction: Taking Grain Into Store Under a Storage Agreement
content:
Grain is taken into store on the scale ticket, and the ticket is what fixes the bushels, the grade and the day. This standing instruction governs deposits under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Standing instruction

1. Bushels are taken into store only while the agreement stands in active or in load-out, so grain arriving against an agreement not yet accepted is held in open storage in the member's name until it is.

2. The storage start date is the day the first bushels go into store under the agreement, and it is never reset by later deposits, so a member who tops a bin up in January still carries the free-day and escalation clocks from the first load in October.

3. The elevation charge for taking grain in is raised on the bushels of that load at the programme's rate, and is taken once per load rather than once per agreement.

4. A deposit below the programme's minimum deposit is not refused but is taken into open storage instead, because the programme's rates are written against a working minimum.

5. Grain arriving out of condition is dried before it is credited into store, so the bushels credited are the bushels after conditioning shrink and not the bushels across the scale.

## The standing test in paragraph 1

The standing that admits a deposit is read off the cooperative's own record of the agreement, matched to the scale ticket the load came in on, and read before the bushels are credited. Two standings admit a deposit: active, and in load-out. An agreement still in applied standing, one on billing hold, one closed and one terminated do not admit it, and grain arriving against any of them is held in open storage in the member's name.

## Positive and negative cases, on hypothetical loads

**Positive.** A member's agreement stands active. Two loads arrive on separate tickets in the same week. Both are credited into store, and elevation in is raised twice, once on the bushels of each load.

**Positive.** The agreement is in load-out, with an order being worked. A load arriving that day is still credited into store, load-out standing being one of the two that admit a deposit.

**Negative.** The member signed the application last week and the agreement still stands in applied standing. A load arriving today is taken into open storage in the member's name rather than credited under the agreement.

**The start date.** First bushels went in on 14 October and a further load arrived on 7 January. The storage start date remains 14 October for both the free-day clock and the escalation clock.
